The task extractor is a rule-based stand-in that can only find what the app sends it (args.content / args.openTasks), so the app's own request, cut, merge and storage are what is judged, not the model. Spec ext-tc22-s27-other-charts.spec.ts, 13/13 judged. Four charts (A, B Hospital; R, R2 Nursing Home) with the same three tasks. Then on R: R closes and gets the diet task, R2 deep-equals its seed, A and B unchanged; both Task Exports scoped by name. Whether the live model closes A's tasks is S01/S03's dev half; nothing a model answers can reach another chart, since the request carries only this chart's tasks.

SES requests are signed by the code itself and built as `https://${host}` with host = email.<region>.amazonaws.com; AWS_SES_REGION or AWS_REGION only picks the region, never the scheme (ses.ts:39/89/101/120). - **SDK default (https):** Bedrock uses a BedrockRuntimeClient with no endpoint set (bedrock.ts:85). Vertex uses a GoogleGenAI client with vertexai=true and no base URL (vertex.ts:150). OpenAI chat and vision use `new OpenAI({ apiKey })` with no baseURL (openai.ts:92). Live-session key minting calls client.realtime.clientSecrets.create on an OpenAI client with no baseURL (transcribe.ts:71-74). Each of these can still be redirected by an env var the SDK reads itself: OPENAI_BASE_URL, AWS_ENDPOINT_URL / AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME, and the GenAI SDK's base-URL vars. - **Built from an env var:** the Specode relay does fetch(SPECODE_EMAIL_RELAY_URL) (email.ts:18/25). It only runs when AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER is not "ses" and SPECODE_EMAIL_MODE is "platform"; when AUTH_EMAIL_PROVIDER=ses it is never reached. The scheme-relevant http:// literal in the code is the dev fallback `process.env.SITE_URL ?? "http://localhost:5173"` (auth.ts:105). The backend never fetches that value. The web client keeps the session cookie in localStorage with an expiry computed from Max-Age (12 h idle) and the device clock, and drops it once the device clock passes that date. Breaks UAT 3.8 ('A phone with a wrong clock, no clock set, or a different time zone shows the same state as any other device') and the S07 oracle for U3/U4 ('a sign-out caused only by the browser clock = Fail'). statusMessage:
probes: failed → failed · product (failed · product (the lane flagged a product issue))
Re-checked after review 2026-10-14 (18:00 JST runs: fix-*.json). NH: going offline inside the 800 ms autosave keeps a device copy (one put, no delete); (b) F is restored on the phone and reaches the computer, draft row gone after the echo; (a) the computer's later G wins and F is dropped silently (record-only, Q11). Hospital: the probe (every put/delete on the draft store, init script) shows the copy IS written with a valid key while offline (so the session / draftId is not null) and deleted 4–7 ms later, still offline, while the server never had F; after the page closes F is gone: (b) neither the phone, the computer nor the server has it; (a) G shown, F gone. Cause, from the probe + code: Hospital saves through rounding.update with an optimistic update (src/routes/rounding/Patient.tsx:33) that patches the local chart at once, so useAutosave's 'server echoed my text' check (src/lib/useAutosave.ts:101-110) fires locally and deletes the copy before anything reached the server; Nursing Home saves without one and keeps the copy. That path is local and does not depend on how the network is cut, so it should hold on a real phone in airplane mode — still worth one device check.
Product issue: Hospital pre-round (and every Hospital autosave field that saves through the same optimistic rounding.update): a line typed just before the phone loses signal (within the 0.8 s autosave) is lost if the app is closed before the signal returns — on reopening, the pre-round notes and the computer show nothing of it, while the same flow in Nursing Home restores it. The device copy is written and then deleted at once by the local optimistic echo (Patient.tsx:33 + useAutosave.ts:101-110), before the server has the text. Breaks Empty & Failure States 'nothing typed is lost' (TC-25 S28 b).

Real clock vs page.clock +2 d vs Pacific/Kiritimati with the device clock pinned to 11:00 UTC (UTC+14 date Oct 15 while UTC and Tokyo are Oct 14), plus a control with the same pinned clock in Tokyo. Breaks TC-02 S13b and ground rule 3.8.

statusMessage:
Re-verdict after the QA review of TFA-94422 (2026-10-14; not yet checked by Quinn): passed. The two 'premise not met' notes were the check reading the backend about 12 s after Generate started. Timestamps show the chart was left while generating (about 1.3 s / 1.6 s) and the note was stored at about 4 s / 4.7 s, so the premise held. The check should compare noteGeneratedAt, the time of leaving and encounterEditedAt.
newspec-c: passed → passed (passed)
PW, local stack, both modes (generateNote mocked, answered 8 s after it is asked, so A's note lands while B is open). A: dictation typed, Generate, then the app's back arrow and the list to B at once (no reload); B has its own encounter line. B's Post-Round right after opening and 45 s later and B's Encounter tab show nothing of A; B's stored note is empty and its encounter text is exactly its own line; back on A the Encounter tab holds A's dictation, the stored text equals it, and A's Post-Round shows A's own note. Judged 7/7 per mode. Every Generate used a 'procedure-other' custom note template because on 43c38a4f saving a generated note queues a server billing job (billing/persistence.ts enqueueBilling → ai/billing.ts run) that no socket mock can answer and that would reach Bedrock on this stack; the template only changes the (mocked) model's instruction text. Tripwire: no model call at all during the run.
